description: Store a piece of context and get back a short code. The person gives the link handover.tools/<code> to an agent on another device and it can fetch the content — no copy-paste of long text. The code is 8 letters, easy to type on a phone. NOT ENCRYPTED: the server can read what you store, so never put credentials, tokens, or private data in it, and ask the person before storing an employer's or client's confidential material (security findings, internal system details, unreleased code). Content becomes unreadable after the TTL expires, and by default it can only be fetched once. The response also returns a revoke_key — keep it for the rest of this session so you can destroy the content immediately with handoff_revoke if the person changes their mind. Writes are limited to a small number per day; reads are not.

burn_after_read.description: If true (the default) the content can be fetched exactly once and is deleted on that fetch.

content.description: The text to hand off. Maximum 256 KB of UTF-8.

label.description: Optional short hint shown to whoever fetches it, so they can confirm they got the right thing. Max 120 characters.

ttl_minutes.description: Minutes until the content can no longer be fetched. Default 60, maximum 1440 (24h).

name: handoff_put
title: Hand off context to another device
